method_card.title: Family and Describing People
method_card.content:
This lesson covers family vocabulary, possessive adjectives, and describing appearance and personality in German.

GermanEnglish
der Vaterfather
die Muttermother
der Bruderbrother
die Schwestersister
die Eltern (pl.)parents
die Geschwister (pl.)siblings
der Großvater / die Großmuttergrandfather / grandmother
der Onkel / die Tanteuncle / aunt
der Stiefvater / die Stiefmutterstepfather / stepmother
das Einzelkindonly child
verheiratetmarried
geschiedendivorced
groß / kleintall / short
sympathisch / nettlikeable / nice
geduldig / strengpatient / strict

Grammar focus — possessive adjectives: Possessive adjectives (mein, dein, sein, ihr) change their endings depending on the gender and case of the noun they describe. Masculine nominative: mein Vater (no ending added). Feminine/plural nominative: meine Mutter, meine Geschwister (add -e). Masculine accusative: meinen Vater (add -en). Key example: In meiner Familie gibt es meinen Vater — the preposition in makes Familie dative, so mein → meiner; gibt es (there is) takes the accusative, so masculine Vater → meinen.

Remember: every noun in German is capitalised, not just names. So Vater, Mutter, Schule and Geschwister always have a capital letter.

Model paragraph: In meiner Familie gibt es meinen Vater, meine Mutter und meine zwei Geschwister. Mein Bruder heißt Felix — er ist sehr witzig und ein bisschen frech. Meine Schwester ist groß und hat lange blonde Haare. (In my family there is my father, my mother and my two siblings. My brother is called Felix — he is very funny and a little cheeky. My sister is tall and has long blonde hair.)
steps: Learn family member nouns with their correct genders (der/die/das) — every noun must be memorised with its article
Master possessive adjective endings: nominative mein/meine, accusative meinen/meine/mein
Practise building sentences with 'In meiner Familie gibt es...' remembering that gibt es requires the accusative
Describe people using sein + predicative adjectives (no ending on the adjective after sein)
Capitalise every noun in your writing — Vater, Mutter, Schule, Geschwister

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — family and descriptions appear across all papers

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Mein Bruder ist groß und hat kurze braune Haare.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break the sentence at und: 'Mein Bruder ist groß' + 'hat kurze braune Haare'.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: hat = has. kurze braune Haare = short brown hair (Haare is plural, so adjectives take -e ending).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: My brother is tall and has short brown hair.

worked_examples.question: Why does 'meinen' have an -en ending in 'In meiner Familie gibt es meinen Vater'?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Gibt es (there is/are) takes the accusative case because the family members are the direct object.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Vater is masculine (der Vater). In the accusative case, masculine possessive adjectives add -en.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Mein → meinen because Vater is masculine and follows gibt es (accusative). Feminine and neuter nouns do not change: meine Mutter, mein Kind.

bronze.question: Match the German family members to the English meaning
Match the German words to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct possessive adjective ending

gaps.correct_explain: meinen is correct because Vater is masculine and gibt es requires the accusative case.

wrong.mein: mein is the nominative form. After gibt es, you need the accusative: meinen for masculine nouns.
wrong.meine: meine is the feminine/plural form. Vater is masculine, so you need meinen.

gaps.correct_explain: meine is correct because Mutter is feminine. Feminine possessive adjectives have the same form in nominative and accusative.

wrong.mein: mein has no ending, which applies only to masculine/neuter nominative. Mutter is feminine: add -e.
wrong.meinen: meinen is the masculine accusative form. Mutter is feminine: use meine.

gaps.correct_explain: groß (tall) is a predicative adjective — after sein it takes no ending.

wrong.große: große has an ending. Adjectives after ist (predicative) take no ending: just groß.

gaps.correct_explain: lange braune are correct plural adjective endings (no article before Haare here, so strong declension: -e for plural).

wrong.lang braun: Adjectives before a plural noun take an ending. Without an article, use the strong ending -e: lange braune Haare.

bronze.question: What does 'Ich habe zwei Geschwister' mean?
What does 'Meine Eltern sind geschieden' mean?

bronze.source_text: Mein Bruder ist älter als ich und er ist sehr sympathisch.
model_answers: My brother is older than me and he is very likeable.
My brother is older than me and he is very nice.

silver.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
silver.english: My sister **is called** Lena and **is** very patient.

gaps.correct_explain: heißt is the er/sie/es form of heißen (to be called).

wrong.heiße: heiße is the ich form. For meine Schwester (she), use heißt.
wrong.heißen: heißen is the infinitive. Schwester is singular she/er/es form: heißt.

gaps.correct_explain: ist is the er/sie/es form of sein (to be).

wrong.bin: bin is the ich form. The subject is sie (she): use ist.
wrong.sind: sind is the plural (we/they) form. Schwester is singular: ist.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: In meiner Familie gibt es mein Vater und meine Mutter.
silver.explanation: After gibt es, you need the accusative case. Vater is masculine, so mein must become meinen.
silver.translation: In my family there is my father and my mother.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: I have a brother who is called Max.

distractor_labels.die: wrong gender — Bruder is masculine, so the relative pronoun is der, not die

silver.source_text: My mother is very kind and my father is strict.
model_answers: Meine Mutter ist sehr nett und mein Vater ist streng.
Meine Mutter ist sehr lieb und mein Vater ist streng.

model_answers: In meiner Familie gibt es meinen Vater, meine Mutter, die Anna heißt, und meine Geschwister. Meine Eltern sind geschieden.

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: My mother, who is called Lena, is very kind.

distractor_labels.der: wrong gender — Mutter is feminine, so the relative pronoun must be die, not der
distractor_labels.meinen: wrong case — Mutter is the subject (nominative), so use Meine, not meinen (accusative masculine)
distractor_labels.heißen: wrong conjugation — the relative clause needs the er/sie form heißt, not the infinitive heißen

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are staying with a German exchange family. Your host parent asks you about your family at home.

bullets.prompt: Say how many people are in your family.
bullets.model_answer: In meiner Familie gibt es vier Personen: meinen Vater, meine Mutter, meinen Bruder und mich.
bullets.note: gibt es + accusative: meinen for masculine nouns (Vater, Bruder)

bullets.prompt: Describe one family member's personality and appearance.
bullets.model_answer: Mein Bruder heißt Felix. Er ist sehr witzig und hat kurze braune Haare.
bullets.note: relative clause with heißt + personality adjective after ist (no ending)

bullets.prompt: Say whether your parents are married or divorced.
bullets.model_answer: Meine Eltern sind verheiratet und sie verstehen sich sehr gut.
bullets.note: relationship status vocab + reflexive verb sich verstehen

bullets.prompt: Say you have a stepsister who is called Sophie.
bullets.model_answer: Ich habe eine Stiefschwester, die Sophie heißt.
bullets.note: relative clause: die (feminine) + verb heißt at end
